quest.title: The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call
quest.description: In order to look for more information about your sibling, you and Paimon decide to visit Nahida in the Sanctuary of Surasthana once more. Along the way, you hear people discussing something...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Prepare yourselves. I'm going to transport you into Irminsul.

talks.objective: Go to the Sanctuary of Surasthana

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: Come on, serious suggestions, please. I'm not trying to write a thriller here! It's supposed to be an essay, you understand? An essay. That means facts and logic.

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: Well, if it's facts and logic you're after, you shot yourself in the foot with your choice of research topic, didn't you? "The Tatarasuna Mystery"... When so much remains unexplained, there's little to be objective about. Unless, of course, you restrict yourself to textual criticism.

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: Yeah, well... This is my teacher's area of research. I can't change that. But it's fascinating enough without having to sensationalize it, don't you think? The strange location, the missing details, a mysterious person...

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: I want to write my essay on something interesting, and I'm interested in getting to the bottom of all this. That's the only reason I came to you!

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: Yes, you came to me, so all the more reason to take my advice! The fact is, it's the dramatization that will make people want to read it. There's no getting around that.

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: Uh... Okay, but...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did one of them just mention Tatarasuna? But that's all the way in Inazuma...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it just Paimon, or is it kinda unusual for someone in Sumeru to wanna write a paper about that? ...Huh, everyone here's just going about their business — maybe it really is just Paimon. Guess people here are free to research pretty much anything.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Still, let's go listen in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! Let's go find out what this "Tatarasuna Mystery" is all about.

talks.objective: Talk to the scholars by the road

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: Alright, I guess I'll go with my textual criticism and your editorial direction for the first draft. I have a feeling that the missing kabukimono will end up being the main focus of this paper.

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: #*sigh* If only we knew where to find that Traveler... From what they say about {F#her}{M#him}, this seems like the kind of thing {M#he}{F#she}'d know about.

choices.text: Looking for me?

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Oh, you're the Traveler, you say? Hmm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what's with that face? Don't believe us?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If you don't believe me, I'll go.

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: No, no! Of course I believe you. Actually, I first heard about your great exploits when I was still in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: This is my first time coming face-to-face with you and your mysterious silver-haired companion... I couldn't believe my luck, and out of force of habit, I started, uh, examining the evidence... Sorry.

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Sawada, for the love of... Haha, sorry, we don't get out much, so our social skills are kinda lacking...

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Traveler, I hear you've helped many people a great deal, and been to many places. Would you be able to tell us about Tatarasuna?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, we don't know much about that place either. In fact, we only came over here 'cause we heard YOU talking about it, and wanted to learn more.

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Ah... I see.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sorry I can't help this time.

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: My teacher chose this area of research as a personal challenge. He said it's difficult to get into, because even Inazumans don't know much about Tatarasuna's past. But who'd have thought that—

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: If you don't mind, I'd love to show you all my outline for the book I'm writing about Tatarasuna.

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Hold on, Sawada. Don't you think that's a bit of a deep dive for a first read?

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Fair point. In that case, please ease yourselves in gently by taking a look at Aqaba's latest essay draft.

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Let me give you some background. This all started with the discovery of some records in Tatarasuna. The writings mentioned someone by the name of "Mikoshi Nagamasa," who crafted a fine blade.

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: But in the end, he threw it into a fire to destroy it, and killed his servant, Katsuragi. Why? Well. No one knows.

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Apart from the sword-maker, his servant, and the one who wrote this all down, the records also mention a "kabukimono." This seems to be an Inazuman word for an eccentric stranger — someone who dresses funny or acts in an unusual way.

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: That's right. Aqaba's teacher has spent quite some time researching these events on the ground. This kabukimono lived in Tatarasuna for a while before disappearing without a trace, and shortly afterwards... as Aqaba mentioned, things got pretty ugly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So first the strange person goes missing, then a murder happens? Hmm, seems kinda fishy to Paimon!

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Yes, my thoughts exactly! So I helped out too. I asked everyone I could think of if they knew anything about what happened back then... and WOW, did I get LUCKY!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Stop shouting!

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: This part's important. I just wanted to make it stand out.

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: It just so happens that a friend of mine works at the government records office. He looked into it for me, and I can now confirm that all the aforementioned individuals did, in fact, live in Inazuma over four hundred years ago.

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Even back then, Tatarasuna was already at the center of Inazuma's smelting industry. The man in charge was a government official named Niwa. Curiously enough, it seems like he went missing, too.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Could it be...!)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so there are TWO missing people in this story now?

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: That's right! What's more, "Niwa" is a name with a lot of history to it. Have you ever heard of the great swordsmith clans of Inazuma?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, the swordsmiths? Yeah, umm... like Isshin Art and so on?

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Wow, yes, you really know your stuff. That makes things easier. So basically, this Niwa was a distant relative of the Kaedehara Clan — the last practitioners of Isshin Art.

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Something then seems to have happened in the Kaedehara Clan leading to their downfall... I don't know the details, but taken in light of everything else going on around that time, it makes you wonder whether it's all connected somehow...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...The Kaedehara Clan...

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: ...Sawada, you left out the biggest detail of all!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's more!?

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Oh! Yes, of course, how could I forget! Brace your minds, ladies and gents, for they are about to be blown. Or maybe you won't believe your ears... I wouldn't blame you, of course, because in all my years as a writer, this is by far the most—

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Get to the point, for Pete's sake!

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: ...According to information acquired by Aqaba's teacher, the kabukimono was not a human... But a puppet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A puppet?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The Shogun puppet that the Electro Archon made should be ruling Inazuma with her as we speak... It couldn't be her.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The kabukimono has to be The Balladeer, but... what was he doing 400 years ago in Tatarasuna?)

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Aha! Judging by the looks on your faces, you do know something after all?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Uhh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Glare at Paimon and hope she keeps her mouth shut.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, no! Paimon just meant... "Uhh, how creepy!" The way you described it makes it sound like a ghost story!

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: I agree. It does, but considering that non-human races in Inazuma are by no means uncommon, spooky events are to be expected... And that's exactly what my book is about — please, take a look.

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Oh, and please read my essay draft as well!

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Sawada was encouraging me to follow his more creative approach, but I think essays should be grounded in facts. I don't think explaining everything away with mysterious forces will cut it...

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Ooh, how about if I plug the holes in Sawada's narrative with political intrigue? Like, um, I could put a turf war between rival factions at the center of the whole series of events.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you're allowed to just make stuff up? Pretty sure you've gone from "essay" to "guessay" there.

choices.text: Yeah, sounds more like a novel...

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Aqaba, look... Your teacher has researched this extensively. I've reached out to everyone I could think of... Whatever information we have now is all that there is to know. This is as much detail as you're ever going to get.

response.speaker: Sawada
response.text: Besides, if there really was a political power struggle going on at anything like the level you seem to be suggesting, what hope would we ever have of finding out the truth?

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: ...Ugh, good point. Okay, back to the drawing board, I guess... Gimme some time. I need to find a new angle on this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll leave you to it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We have some other stuff to do, so we'll have to say goodbye for now. Good luck with your essay!

response.speaker: Aqaba
response.text: Alright, thank you. If you find out any more info about all this, please do let me know! Thanks so much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, so that thing they were talking about... It has to do with The Balladeer, doesn't it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay... Then, even if we did know something about it, we probably couldn't share it with them, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After all, we kicked his butt and got him locked up. Information about people like that is usually super confidential, isn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you ask Paimon, Aqaba should just pick a different topic. There must be as many essay topics as there are trees in the forest. There's no point in—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aah!!!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's wrong!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, did you see that? He literally just went by. Over there... it looked like, like...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Balladeer!? No it can't have been, he got locked up... Quick, let's catch up and see!

choices.text: (Has this guy ever even written an essay before?)
If you're looking for the Traveler, that's me.

talks.objective: Follow the figure you just saw

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, there you are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida, bad news! We just saw The Balladeer, strolling around in public!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did he escape, or...? ...Aah! It's him!

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Hmph. Sure enough, you're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what are you doing in the Sanctuary of Surasthana!? Aren't you supposed to be locked up!?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I know you must have a lot of questions. Please, allow me to explain.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It was my idea to set The Balladeer free. We made a deal, and he's gonna do some investigation in Irminsul for me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A deal!? You sure you trust this guy?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: What did you expect? Why do you think Sumeru would keep me around otherwise? ...Or maybe killing me is all you can think about?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: But if that's the case, why haven't you done it already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't flatter yourself. It was... Nahida said there's still some mysteries in you to figure out!

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Ah, so if it were up to you, you'd finish the job? Guess I had you all wrong. There I was thinking you were just getting cold feet.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Ugh, well that escalated quickly. Not a good start... Could I ask you all to please calm down?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon's worried about you, Nahida! Don't let him trick you!

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Haha, it's not every day you see people questioning the God of Wisdom's judgment. Just when you think you've seen it all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't you dare try to drive a wedge between us!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As long as the terms are reasonable, I don't think there's a problem in making a deal. Even with The Balladeer.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Well, I for one have no reason to doubt you, considering you even struck a deal with The Doctor.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, one in which I gained valuable information. You'll come to understand more about that in the fullness of time.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Balladeer's power was all but completely spent after your battle. He's no longer strong enough to be a strategic threat to us. That puts him in quite a precarious position.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Plus, he's a former Harbinger with knowledge of many of the Fatui's sensitive secrets. Being stuck here in Sumeru could make him a sitting duck, depending on how the Fatui plan to respond.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a second... former? You mean, he's not a Harbinger anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I take no pleasure in saying this, but... it seems as if The Doctor had no intention of welcoming back a loser, so...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...So he tossed you out like trash.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Sometimes it's you using them, other times it's them using you. Most human relationships are this way... certainly all the stable ones are. That's how it was between me and the Fatui, and also between each of the Harbingers.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: So as long as you have some value to offer, nobody will ever abandon you. But after recent events, even I have to admit that I'm not worth quite what I used to be...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Really? What a crying shame.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: ...Hmph, well, if the Fatui are gonna re-evaluate my utility, I need to have a backup plan for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As we discussed, I don't like causing harm to living beings, and you said you need protection. So, why not join forces with us?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I think these two have made their objection to that idea fairly clear, don't you? And they're your friends, so I guess you'll be siding with them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, obviously! Nahida, don't listen to him!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Then let's put that discussion to the side for now. We still have time.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Today can be a trial run. Where we go from here will depend on how well we manage to cooperate today.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Alright. Then I'll do what we agreed.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Good. Go now, and keep in touch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida, are you... are you serious about this?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #I have my reasons for this decision. In fact... I'm largely doing it for your benefit, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...For me?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes. As I told you once before, there's information about your twin in Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah. Actually, that's the whole reason we came to see you today. So you have an update on that?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. You may remember me mentioning that the Fatui had not included your twin's details in the "Descender" category. This is an extremely important point.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's possible that the Fatui have other information that even I don't know about. And since The Balladeer used to be one of them, he'll be better acquainted with this information than I am.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: He was granted the power to connect with Irminsul when he almost became the god of a new era. Even though he no longer has the Gnosis, some traces of its power remain in him. He can still connect.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The amount of information in Irminsul is vast beyond description. Sifting through all of it without knowing what to look for would take too long, even for me.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So I asked The Balladeer to search in Irminsul for any information about the Descenders. He's more familiar with this kind of information, and should be able to find it more quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What if he lies to you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! Or what if... Paimon just doesn't trust him. He's treated us as enemies every time we've run into him.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I understand, but sometimes, everything is dictated by which side you're on.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #How things will go in the future depends on what information he brings back. And {NICKNAME}... I know what your heart desires most of all.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Our minds have connected several times before. There is a corner of your heart reserved for an intense longing... A feeling of being all alone in the dark, searching for the one candle whose light still burns.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As Sumeru's deity, it is my responsibility to be on guard against The Balladeer. But as someone who counts you as a friend, I want to do something for you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: If this deal with The Balladeer can give you the answers you've been longing to find, then it's worth it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Thank you, Nahida.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's my pleasure, really. You're Sumeru's hero! You've more than earned it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Paimon's still worried about this idea... Is there anything we can do to help?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I was going to contact you about that, but then you suddenly showed up of your own accord. Seems like we have a telepathic connection.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In fact, I was going to ask you to supervise The Balladeer on my behalf while he carries out the task I assigned.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Even though he only has a fraction of his full power left, that's still a fraction of a former Harbinger. If you could accompany him, it would put my mind at ease.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Of course, I'll be there to help guide you through Irminsul from the outside.

choices.text: Got it.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Great. Thank you.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Prepare yourselves. I'm going to transport you into Irminsul.

choices.text: I'm glad to be able to help.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Look at that, hot on my heels. You know, you didn't have to cut your catch-up short just to keep me company. Oh, but I guess you panicked when you realized that I might enter Irminsul ahead of you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nahida sent me to babysit you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shut your beak, jailbird! No way a prisoner gets to be so smug!

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I understand that prisoners have to put up with harassment from the guards, but right now, I'm on temporary release, so maybe you should think about backing off a little.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Sounds like a successful rendezvous.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I need to be quite clear about something. In a few moments, you'll be entering into the innermost region of Irminsul. It is an environment like no other, and the most important place in all of Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Unlike anywhere else, Irminsul's inner region consists exclusively of torrents of information. You must put aside your differences and be extremely careful as you navigate your way through.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I know there are many grievances between you on both sides, but it is essential that you remain calm after entry. This is as much for your own safety as anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Fine, let's call a truce, but only until this mission's over...

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Let's cut each other a little slack, shall we? We are gonna be traveling together, after all.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Per my agreement with Lesser Lord Kusanali, I'll be at the front. It's my job to lead the way and get rid of any obstacles in our path. All you have to do is keep your pretty eyes open and try not to fall behind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ha! You sure are confident, Paimon'll give you that. You make it sound like you're even more experienced at adventuring than us!

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: If there are no further objections, I suggest we get going.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Or did you need some time to mentally prepare yourselves?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You...! Ugh! The snark on this guy! It's unbearable!

choices.text: There's no need for all the biting sarcasm.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: ...Hmph.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: We can start now.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Irminsul access granted. Initiating connection procedure...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this a small sapling?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Argh, darn it! C'mon, let's catch up with him!

choices.text: Focus on doing your job.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... So this is the inside of Irminsul...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's different than what I imagined...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh... Paimon's never seen anything like this. And it feels like a sacred place...

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Irminsul is closely intertwined with the entirety of Teyvat. Every bit of information flowing here means something.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Pick your jaws up off the floor. It's time to go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why is it that Paimon just wants to do the opposite of everything he says...

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali, we will now proceed to the heart of Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Can you still sense where the heart of Irminsul is?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Yes. Permission to begin searching for information there?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Permission granted. Go ahead.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Let's go. Stay close, don't go running off.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, so... say we did go running off in here, what would happen?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What are you smirking at?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I was just imagining the look on your travel companion's face if you went and got lost.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Anything's possible in here — you can't rule anything out. So if you wanna stay safe, your best option is to stick close to me.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: We're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a huge tree...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is the center of Irminsul. All the information in the world is flowing through it...)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Good, you made it. Are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Ready when you are.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Then please begin. Preparing to access cognitive currents. Establishing waypoint...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Balladeer's actually doing what Nahida tells him... Guess he must want to stay alive.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He hasn't put up any resistance, and he seems good at working on the frontline... Maybe he had a similar role in the Fatui?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (First Aqaba and Sawada's stories, now this... What a strange individual.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The rest is up to you. If you discover anything at all, make sure to share it with us.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Will do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... For once, we're the ones with nothing to do...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #({NICKNAME}, Paimon, would you like to talk?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Nahida? ...Is this a telepathic conversation?)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (Yes. I've also invited Paimon to join.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Huh? ...What the... We can talk to each other inside our heads?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I'm guessing that you don't want us to disturb The Balladeer.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (Hehe, that's part of it. Plus, we're all friends. There's nothing wrong with us talking like this once in a while.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Paimon's never tried this before. This is great!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (So, Paimon's been wanting to ask you something. Don't you think The Balladeer's a bit of a walking contradiction? He's always talking back, but he seems to listen to what you say...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Yes, and he seems to excel at doing odd jobs for others...)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (As I've told you before, there are still some mysteries for him to resolve. Things that are clear as day to me, but that he has yet to understand.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (Perhaps today will be the day that he finds some answers.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is it about his past? The "betrayals"? And the other events in Inazuma?)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (Well done. Smart and attentive as always.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Actually, I caught a glimpse of a few things when I ran into Haypasia at Pardis Dhyai...)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You relate what you saw in The Balladeer's mind while in Pardis Dhyai...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (So you made contact with that part of his mind... Well, it's true. Betrayal turned The Balladeer into the person he is today.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Huh, Paimon thought nothing could get under that guy's skin. Turns out he can get hurt and angry just like anyone else.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (Everyone has a history, Paimon. Even if you're a puppet created by the Electro Archon.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Speaking of puppets, we ran into two people at the Akademiya today talking about an essay. Turns out their topic was about the Tatarasuna incident... Nahida, do you know anything about that?)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (If you mean the mysterious events, the kabukimono, and so on... Yes, I know about all of that.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Really? Because from what they were saying, it sounded like lots of Tatarasuna's history is still unexplained, and most of the information we have now is just from people filling the gaps with their imagination. At least, that's what they thought...)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Nahida about the story Aqaba and Sawada are writing...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (...Oh? How interesting. Those two managed to deduce quite a lot through guesswork alone.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (So the guessay got it right!?)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (Well, they guessed right about one thing: Tatarasuna was sabotaged.)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Must be a riveting conversation you three are having. Funny how all the good ones happen when I'm not involved.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Wh—What makes you think we're talking to each other?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Don't insult me. You're having a private conversation without me. Obviously, I must be the topic of said conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We have every right to keep certain things confidential.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Of course you do. You can't have your prisoner knowing too much.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, uh, have you found anything yet?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Still looking. Don't get your hopes up, though. You and your twin come from outside this world. It wouldn't surprise me if there was nothing on either of you in Irminsul at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait, how'd you know about that? Did Nahida tell you?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: It's not like we've never met before. And anyway, you're world-famous. It'd be more surprising if I didn't know a few things about you.

choices.text: Every conversation with you is hard work...

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Right now, we have to keep the peace. I'm not interested in creating more misery for myself, and making cordial conversation is something I can manage.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: ...Huh? Wait...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This light... It looks similar to those saplings. What could it be?

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: ...Anonymous data?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Don't you forget the agreement. You have to share it with us!

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Shush. Just wait.
...Mr. Niwa, are you certain this is worth the risk? We are talking about Tatarasuna's furnace, after all. It may not pay to act rashly...
There's no one else who can enter the furnace. It has to be me.
Is that so...? *sigh* Well, since you insist...

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: *gasp*... It's...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (That name... Niwa was the man in charge at Tatarasuna. Plus, he belongs to the lineage of Isshin Art...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa!

choices.text: ...But your attitude is better than I thought.

talks.objective: Investigate the fragments of information from Irminsul

dialogues.text: I have been in Tatarasuna for some time now. You have shown me great hospitality, as has Mikoshi Nagamasa... and indeed, everyone else.
Under your leadership, Tatarasuna is a warm, welcoming place, like a giant village. People are gainfully employed, their lives have purpose. They are motivated.

As I understand, the Raiden Shogun has, in recent years, eliminated much of the evil that plagued Inazuma. As for Tatarasuna, it was originally established as a means of safely disposing Crystal Marrow.
The forging industry with Crystal Marrow as a raw material has since flourished, giving rise to generations of swordsmiths — some world-renowned, others unknown... all passing on their legacy.
Skills, blood, dreams... Every smith brought into this trade looks to find their purpose between steel and blade. That is why you accepted the proposal brought to you by myself and Akame.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: Yes, well... Were it not for you coming to Inazuma and happening to make Akame's acquaintance, the two of you never would have joined forces. And he would be the first to admit that there's no way he could have revolutionized our forging process like this on his own — at least not on the same timescale.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: You allowed Akame to take all the credit for a method that you jointly developed, he sold it to me, and now, every piece of ore here is smelted using the new technique.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: Even now, you remain one of Tatarasuna's key consultants, working right here alongside us. I believe it is you, Sir, who are truly responsible for the changes in our manufacturing and forging methods.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: You flatter me. From the outset, I saw much that was commendable in the forging industry of Inazuma, and it has been my great honor to befriend you all.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: So you say, Escher... But is this really the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: My good sir, what do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: ...I tried to resist thinking it was all connected because I didn't want to speculate, and I didn't want to believe that things could turn out this way.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: What have we gained from adopting your new technology? Ominous, black smoke, mounting production problems... Worker fatigue and casualties are up, and continuing to rise at an alarming rate.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: And recently, as you well know, someone died because of that strange filth inside the furnace. We've kept the truth from spreading outside, but still, I suspect you understand it better than I do.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: None of the people who went out to get help have come back. Now, our mutual friend, the kabukimono, is taking the golden feather to Narukami Island to seek an audience with the Shogun. This is our last hope.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: But that doesn't faze you, does it, Escher? Nothing does... Otherwise, why would you still be standing there with that smile on your face?

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: I'm just surprised that you finally chose to be so sincere. I'm sure you've been harboring these suspicions for quite some time.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: Mikoshi Nagamasa may have noticed that there was one common denominator among all these events... namely you, Escher. But Mr. Mikoshi is more cautious than I. He does things by the book.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: After all, Nagamasa is the adopted son of Mikoshi Torachiyo, the youkai struck down by the Shogun's own hand. If he truly seeks to redeem his family's honor, an abundance of caution is well-advised.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: ...You're well-informed on the subtleties of his situation for a mechanic all the way from Fontaine. Are you sure you're not a little overqualified?

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: Why, Mr. Niwa, are you suggesting I find a job as a diplomat? Sadly, I am so very attached to my craft...

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: Enough, Escher.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: I'm here because an evil force is raging inside the furnace, and someone needs to take your new device inside the high-risk zone so we can absorb it and put an end to the problem.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: ...I'm in charge here, and I'm about to take some responsibility and head inside, probably to my death. But what about you? What are you still doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: Judging from the look in your eyes, you don't seem to trust me.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: Drop the act. We're past that now. Whoever you are, it looks like your plan to destroy Tatarasuna has worked.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: I just want to know what you're still doing here. What's left? Don't you have all your answers by now?

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: Honestly, I'm just waiting for the right moment.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: A moment like this where you finish talking and I stop you from entering the furnace.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: Argh! You, you...

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: ...Heh, you're a little smarter than I initially gave you credit for.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: I thought I'd disguised myself exceptionally well, at least for the first few days. But to my surprise, you had your people look into my background right from the start.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: It's a long journey from Inazuma to Fontaine, but that didn't stop them. Eventually, they managed to confirm that Escher was an alias, and that I was not from Fontaine at all.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: And yet, despite all of that, you still fail to realize my true identity, and what I seek in Tatarasuna. Did you really think you would be able to see through my plan?

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: ...Ugh... If you kill me, there's no one who can get inside the furnace... So you're really going to destroy this place... is that it?

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: Oh, but you're quite wrong — there is one other person. Hm, some may not see him as a person, but... you told him yourself: "You're not a puppet. You're a human... you're just missing a heart."

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: Whoever you're working for won't get away with this. They'll be found out. But... this makes no sense. What are you really trying to accomplish by all this? Why go to all this trouble?

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: It's no trouble at all... Patience is a virtue which I have in abundance. This is all part of a carefully controlled experiment.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: If you must know, I am happy to divulge my true identity. I am a Fatui Harbinger. Call me "The Doctor."

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: ...The... Fatui? Who... What do you want...?

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: Just to create a minor inconvenience for your nation.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: That's it? THAT's why you... gave us your cursed technology... just to let loose the evil energy from the Crystal Marrow...

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: Hehe, look how even the righteous soul is filled with venom when faced with its demise.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: My device functions precisely as you say. It is the only chance you have of preventing a catastrophe and keeping the truth from the outside world. However... I did not make it with you in mind.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: It is easier for a person to be possessed by evil spirits when they are filled with hate. So, give in to your fury... I want to see what happens when a malevolent heart is placed into an unsuspecting puppet.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: Make no mistake: Even without you, that pure, innocent puppet would only end up being used by someone else instead. What other reason would a human have for befriending one who is not of our kind?

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: ...*gasping for air*... *gasping for air*... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: If you give him... my heart... tell him that both Nagamasa... and I... see him as... one of us.

dialogues.speaker: Niwa
dialogues.text: He has nothing to prove to anyone... because not everyone... just wants to use other people. The only ones who think like that... are people like you...

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: What a beautiful way to see the world. It almost makes me feel a little guilty... Hm, then out of respect for you, I shall redefine myself.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: Think of me as a monster or a demon, if you wish... At least this way, your death is not a consequence of your own folly turning you into an easy target. You simply lost to something more powerful than you could ever hope to defeat.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: I say, Mr. Niwa, let's see what happens. Will your puppet friend become a human? No, that will prove quite impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: ...Mr. Niwa? ...Tsk, already dead. What a pity.

dialogues.speaker: Escher
dialogues.text: Phew...

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Jester, I have completed the task you gave me. Creating a gap and infiltrating Inazuma's inner workings... Heh, what fun it was.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I'd like to introduce a puppet to you. If he proves useful, let's make him our newest comrade. And if not... let's turn him to dust.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, are you all right?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: ...Dottore? Hahaha... Dottore!!!

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Good, good...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was that The Doctor? Did he... turn into a mechanic from Fontaine?

choices.text: I'm afraid so.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why did we see things from his perspective...?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: When I touched The Doctor to confirm whether he'd eliminated all his segments, I read this memory in his mind. You have to admit, it must be the truth.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Maybe so... But it means nothing.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Does it? But this memory shows that Niwa didn't betray you. He never meant for you to be the one to take the device into the furnace.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You know very well what that means. Even more so than I.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This betrayal was a lie that he has believed for hundreds of years. Was this part of The Doctor's experiment?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (If the betrayal never happened... it existed only in his imagination. But where does this leave him?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's... give him some space. He looks really mad. Paimon doesn't want to be anywhere near him right now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay, let's go over there.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (We need to give him some time to process his emotions.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Paimon's still confused about the Tatarasuna incident. So The Doctor was behind it, but why has that gotten him so worked up?)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (Nobody has ever deceived you like that, Paimon. It's natural that you find it difficult to understand. Perhaps he needed to learn this someday.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (So now you have the complete picture. Katsuragi took the kabukimono to live with the people of Tatarasuna. Later, The Doctor showed up, disguised as a mechanic from Fontaine... and that's when the trouble began.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (It was all a horrific experiment planned by The Doctor... Everything he did was just to plant seeds of disaster in Inazuma that would bear fruit in the future.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (Of all the unwitting participants in The Doctor's experiment, The Balladeer became the main test subject.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (After the events you just saw in that memory, The Doctor put Niwa's heart into the device and handed it to The Balladeer. Then, he instructed him to enter the furnace and absorb all the filth caused by the smelting process.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (The load was far beyond what he expected, but The Balladeer survived... He left the furnace in sheer exhaustion and said to the mechanic: "This device seems to have protected me. What's in it?")

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (The mechanic answered: "Niwa fled this place for fear of punishment, but he left you a gift. He said it's the one thing that you've been looking for... He took it straight from the chest of one of his innocent servants.")

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (The mechanic removed the withered heart from the device as he spoke.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (The Balladeer was stunned that such unthinkable cruelty had brought him the thing he'd been longing for his entire life. A heart acquired through cold-blooded murder is a cursed thing, but it had protected him from the filth...)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (He thought Niwa had completely betrayed him, and yet this very betrayal had ensured his survival. Overwhelmed with anger and sorrow, The Balladeer threw the heart to the ground and left Tatarasuna without looking back.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Holy moly... So The Doctor killed an innocent man and pinned everything on the victim? That's terrible...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Being betrayed and abandoned by a close friend is sure to cause great resentment... Now we know what was behind his decision to take revenge on the Raiden Gokaden a hundred years ago.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But it doesn't mean that vengeance was the right decision...)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (Yes. Only if he understands this can he choose a new path forward.)

choices.text: He was the one behind the Tatarasuna incident.

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: Hmm, I've not given much thought to my target audience yet... Then again, this topic should appeal to readers of all ages, surely?

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: Yeah, whatever you write, it's sure to be a huge hit! Unlike my paper... Essays are a nightmare to write, and barely anyone reads them. Don't get me wrong — the topic's great, I just wish I could find more information on it...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A while later...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sh—Shall we see how he's doing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you all right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a scary expression.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: ...Are you worried about me? If we didn't have such a history, I'd almost think that qualifies me to be your friend.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We just want to make sure this doesn't affect the plan.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: It won't. I'll keep my end of the deal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, are you investigating the stuff we wanna know about?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: That's why we're here.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: But unfortunately, there's no information about the Descenders in Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: If even you can't find anything, that seems to confirm it: Irminsul does not keep records on the Descenders. Anyone who comes from beyond this world is not counted as part of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does that mean we have to leave empty-handed...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not unexpected, but still... thank you.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Don't thank me just yet.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: You look really upset... Heh, well, since Irminsul was a dead end, I guess I can share some other info that might interest you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? About what?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: #The reason why there are records about your {M#sister}{F#brother} in Irminsul... It might have something to do with Khaenri'ah. Apparently, Khaenri'ah was {M#her}{F#his} first destination when {M#she}{F#he} arrived in this world.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: #Plus, {M#she}{F#he} only came to this world because the heavens responded to the summoning.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The heavens... responded?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: #The Jester told me this himself. You can take his word on this. He was a royal mage in Khaenri'ah, and lived with your {M#sister}{F#brother} for a time.

choices.text: The Jester, another Fatui Harbinger...

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: I don't know the details. It's up to you whether you want to believe me. All I can say is, I wouldn't lie to you about this.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Did you get all that, Lesser Lord Kusanali?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes. Astonishing news.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Does this info count towards my mission? It wasn't from Irminsul, but was it valuable?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Very valuable.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Good. In that case... I'll take some time for myself now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What have you done?

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali was right: My power's all but completely spent. Even if I use all of the divine power left in me, I can't sustain this shield for very long.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, I shared a secret with you, and now you owe me. So, in return, I'd like you to answer a question for me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What do you want to know?

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Give me your hand.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: (...Can you hear my voice inside your head?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Are you trying to brainwash me?)

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: (No, I can't do anything like that anymore. At most, all I can do is exchange a few words with you.)

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: (So tell me: In this world, is it possible... to change the past?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait. Why would you ask that...?)

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Done.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What the... What happened? Paimon only saw you hold hands for a second...

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: #Nothing. I was just thanking {M#him}{F#her} for helping me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait, that look... Did he see me hesitate? But that was because I know about Greater Lord Rukkhadevata...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Uh-oh, I think... by not denying it immediately, I gave him the answer he needed...)

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: So long. I suggest you get yourselves out of here quickly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Where are you going? Hey, wait up! Didn't you say not to go running off!?

choices.text: Balladeer! Stop!

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Fast reaction time. But I don't think we'll be seeing each other again.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: From this day forth, the names "Balladeer" and "kabukimono" will cease to exist.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: ...Those who died in Tatarasuna because of me deserve another chance at life.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Balladeer! Don't do anything stupid!

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: You know, I never did like insects. Hordes of the puny things swarming together can be a real nuisance... and I enjoy nothing more than to stamp them out like the pests they are.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: But if a colony of harmless ants isn't threatening anyone, I guess they deserve to be left alone... Luckily, everything can be set right. It's time to solve this once and for all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Balladeer! Balladeeeer!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh, he disappeared! C'mon, we gotta find him somehow!

choices.text: Paimon, we have to stop him!
...Why?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, he's really gone...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...Hello? Can you hear me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, Balladeer, what happened just now? I was suddenly cut off by some kind of power...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was The Balladeer's fault! He... he shut you out.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Nahida everything that happened...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...I didn't think he'd be capable of something like that with so little power left.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Did he keep some of his power hidden when he was defeated? Or... did he achieve something beyond his abilities, and it took everything he had...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where the heck did he go? It's all our fault, we were supposed to keep an eye on him... Sorry, Nahida...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Don't be, it's not your fault. Please let me handle this from here, even though I'm not sure I can solve it.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We're running out of time. Follow my lead and get out of Irminsul as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're out! And we're at... uh, an inn or something?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This is an emergency. I'll have to ask you to stay here for now. Everything's arranged, and nobody will disturb you.

choices.text: No, I want to help you!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm sorry, but this isn't something I need your help with. Leave this one to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: An emergency? How bad is it? Nahida, will you be okay?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Don't worry. If my assessment is correct, though there may be some minor disturbances, it won't lead to a disaster. Please rest and recover your strength here until I say it's safe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Her voice has gone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't shake the feeling that something really big has happened. What do you think The Balladeer meant? And why did he suddenly grab onto you before?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Paimon doesn't remember Greater Lord Rukkhadevata... And The Balladeer's question was a strange one. It's hard to explain in full, and the truth might be very distressing for Paimon...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I'll skip the part about Greater Lord Rukkhadevata for now, and focus on The Balladeer.)

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Paimon what The Balladeer asked you, and what he might have been planning...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He wants to change the past? But... surely that's impossible.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's not easy, that's for sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! You can't just rewrite history. All that stuff happened already in real life!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's like... Umm, imagine Paimon drank all the water in this inn. Even if no one was there to see it, Paimon would sure as heck remember drinking it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, great example.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, so why does Paimon still have a bad feeling about this...? Paimon can't help but feel scared about what he might do...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *whine* Paimon's so confused...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe he wants to erase himself from history.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? ...Aaah!!!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon! Are you okay!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sorry, Paimon accidentally, uh... Aw, it's The Balladeer's fault for causing Paimon all this mental stress!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But erasing yourself from history...? It's unthinkable! Is that really possible in Irminsul?

choices.text: Not necessarily, but... maybe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Whew... Uh-oh, Paimon's head is overheating from trying to understand what he's up to... and it's still not working!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gaaah!!! Paimon's had it with that little brat! He's been nothing but trouble ever since we met him!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no way he'll actually succeed, right? Otherwise... won't everyone who's connected to him be affected too?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Indeed. If The Balladeer does erase himself from Irminsul, many people in Inazuma will be affected... I can't imagine what that situation would look like.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Worst case scenario, it will affect everyone with a connection to the Raiden Gokaden... Kazuha, Ayaka, Ayato... Will this mean that they'll disappear!?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's nothing we can do about it at this point... Hey, have you got any ideas on what we should do next?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like now there's nothing left for us to do but to go to sleep. But Paimon's still so worried! Paimon won't be able to sleep a wink tonight...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Me neither.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So how about, uh... w—we list all our favorite foods to take our mind off things? Heck, if that doesn't work, Paimon's probably gonna collapse of anxiety here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, Paimon'll start. First dish, hmmm... Mondstadt Grilled Fish! Oh, and Chicken-Mushroom Skewers, Tea Break Pancakes, Cream Stew, Sautéed Matsutake...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...And Jueyun Chili Chicken, Almond Tofu, Satisfying Salad...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, ooh, also Adeptus' Temptation, Golden Shrimp Balls, Triple-Layered Consommé, Lotus Seed and Bird Egg Soup, and, and...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Umm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Mm? Huh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon? What's wrong?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... What are we... Wh—What was Paimon supposed to be doing just now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon was, um... talking...? Huh, Paimon suddenly can't remember what she was talking about. What was it, again?

choices.text: You were getting so worried about the situation with The Balladeer...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? The Balladeer...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that a food, too? Huh... Weird name, though...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Paimon doesn't remember The Balladeer!? That must mean... he actually pulled it off?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But how did he have that ability? This doesn't make sense...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong? Your eyes are like saucers... Was it something Paimon said?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No, it's nothing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, The Balladeer... Is that someone's name? 'Cuz it sounds like a nickname or something.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (If this is really happening... I need to know what else has changed.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon, come with me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? Okay, sure! Where are we going?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I want to go back to Inazuma.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Fine by Paimon, but... is everything okay? You're acting like this is an emergency.

Let's get over there first.

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: (I wonder what people will make of the story. Of course, we know it's based on true events, but to the average reader, it might come across as too far-fetched... Hmm...)

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: (After I've finished this essay, I'm gonna get out of Sumeru for a while. It's time for a change of scenery.)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: (...Hmph.)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: ...Dottore, you brazen-faced...! Niwa didn't run from justice... you killed him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You must have a whole bunch of questions after our last conversation with Nahida? Paimon was ready to ask her a million more questions, but... didn't wanna seem too pushy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Like, about these "Descenders." So... does that just mean people like you, who come traveling to Teyvat from someplace else?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And as for your {M#sister}{F#brother}... whew, so many questions. Let's go find Nahida and see what else we can find out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... It looks pretty different here compared to last time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The colors are gentler... Guess that must be because Sumeru's at peace now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks the same in every direction...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This space is indeed unusual... But it seems that The Balladeer is more used to it than I.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The fragments have dissipated, and the space seems to have been affected somehow...
